packs.name: Norway
packs.description: Norwegian sources first: SSB, FHI and Norges Bank, with search tips and known gaps.
packs.summary: Norwegian sources first: SSB and FHI (first-class adapters via search_catalog), Norges Bank for rates/FX. Use for questions about Norway or with no explicit geography.

packs.name: Finland
packs.description: Finnish sources first: Statistics Finland (StatFin), with Eurostat and DBnomics for comparisons.
packs.summary: Finnish sources first: StatFin (Statistics Finland, via search_catalog), Eurostat for EU/NUTS comparisons, DBnomics/ECB for cross-country and euro-area rates. Use for questions about Finland or with no explicit geography.

packs.name: US health surveys (NHIS/MEPS)
packs.description: Individual-level US health data: NHIS and MEPS via IPUMS, direct NCHS files, with honest fallbacks to aggregate sources.
packs.summary: US individual-level health data: IPUMS Health Surveys (NHIS/MEPS, needs a user key), NCHS direct files (NHANES, NHIS one-year CSV, no key), MEPS Stata files, CDC aggregate fallbacks (BRFSS/PLACES); plus BRFSS microdata, NSDUH/SAMHDA (substance use), NVSS + CDC WONDER, HRS (ageing panel), SEER (cancer registry), HCUP (hospital discharge, purchase), CMS DE-SynPUF (synthetic claims for prototyping), MIMIC-IV/eICU (critical care, demo open) and All of Us (enclave). Covers the 2025-26 CDC/NCHS suspensions (PRAMS, NAMCS/NHAMCS). Use for health status, insurance, healthcare use, expenditure, ageing and mortality questions.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: BRFSS
packs.description: CDC's state-representative annual survey of adult chronic-disease risk factors and behaviors.
packs.summary: US state-representative adult health microdata (~400k/yr), open XPT downloads, no key. Best for state-level chronic-disease prevalence; weight with _LLCPWT; 2011 weighting break.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: NSDUH / SAMHDA
packs.description: SAMHSA's national survey of substance use, substance use disorders and mental health, ages 12+.
packs.summary: US person-level substance use and mental health microdata (age 12+), open public-use files (SPSS/SAS/Stata) with click-through access; restricted-use with finer geography needs application. Weight with ANALWT_C; no state identifier in public-use files; treat 2020-21 as a COVID-disrupted break.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: NVSS natality/mortality files
packs.description: CDC/NCHS record-level public-use birth and death files.
packs.summary: Record-level US birth (~3.6M/yr) and death (~3.3M/yr) public-use files, open (identified/geo-detailed versions need application); mirrored at NBER. Distinct from CDC WONDER, which only returns aggregated tabulated cells.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: CDC WONDER
packs.description: CDC's aggregated-query API for mortality, natality and other public health statistics.
packs.summary: CDC's query API returning aggregated, suppressed (<10) tabulated cells — NOT microdata. POST-only with an XML request/response format, no OpenAPI spec; keep automated use to about one query per 2 minutes and confirm the current mortality database id before querying.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: HRS
packs.description: NIA/SSA biennial panel study of US adults aged 50+ covering health, wealth and retirement.
packs.summary: US ageing panel (age 50+ and spouses, biennial since 1992) from NIA/SSA/University of Michigan; public files need free registration, restricted biomarker/genetic/geographic files need application. Start from the RAND HRS Longitudinal File, pre-cleaned and harmonized across 15+ waves.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: HCUP
packs.description: AHRQ's all-payer US hospital administrative discharge data (NIS/NEDS/KID/SID).
packs.summary: The largest US all-payer hospital administrative data (NIS/NEDS/KID/SID) — diagnoses, procedures, charges/costs, length of stay; purchase only (account, training, signed DUA, fee). Weight with DISCWT (TRENDWT for series spanning the 2012 discharge-level redesign); HCUPnet gives a free aggregate alternative.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: MIMIC-IV
packs.description: MIT's de-identified critical-care electronic health record database.
packs.summary: Critical-care EHR microdata from the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology; full access needs PhysioNet credentialing (CITI training, signed DUA, human review), but a ~100-patient demo needs none. Dates are randomly shifted per patient — within-patient intervals are valid, absolute calendar time is not.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: European survey microdata (ESS/SHARE/GESIS)
packs.description: European individual-level surveys: ESS via its open API, plus honest guidance for SHARE, GESIS, WVS/EVS and UKDS.
packs.summary: European individual-level survey data: ESS (machine-reachable API, needs a free user ID) and CESSDA (metadata search) first; SHARE (with easySHARE as the recommended entry point) and its g2aging harmonisation hub, SOEP, Understanding Society, ELSA, TILDA, GGP, GESIS holdings (Eurobarometer/ISSP/ALLBUS/EVS), UK Data Service, WVS, Eurostat EHIS/EU-SILC and LIS — login- or form-walled sources are described honestly with fallbacks to Eurostat/OECD aggregates. Use for attitudes, welfare, health, ageing, values.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: Global development surveys (DHS/WB/barometers)
packs.description: Households and individuals in low- and middle-income countries: DHS indicators, World Bank Microdata search, regional barometers.
packs.summary: Households and individuals in low- and middle-income countries: DHS indicator API and World Bank Microdata Library (wbmicro, metadata search) are machine-reachable and keyless; MICS (UNICEF), WHO STEPS (NADA-based NCD microdata), WHO SAGE, HAALSI (fully open ageing panel), the g2aging LMIC sister studies (CHARLS/LASI/MHAS/KLoSA/JSTAR), World Values Survey, Afrobarometer/Latinobarometro/Arab/Asian Barometer and Global.health; GBD/GHDx flagged as modelled estimates, not microdata. Worldbank/WHO/OWID as aggregate fallback.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: US social surveys (GSS/PUMS/Pew)
packs.description: US attitudes and demographics at the individual level: GSS direct downloads, Census PUMS, and gated Pew data.
packs.summary: US attitudes, demographics and social behavior at the individual level: Census PUMS (ACS/CPS, needs CENSUS_API_KEY) and GSS (open Stata downloads, no key) are machine-reachable; Pew Research is login-walled. For US health surveys, use the separate 'US health surveys' pack instead.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: Education & skills (PIAAC/PISA/TALIS)
packs.description: OECD skills and education microdata: PIAAC per-country CSVs (usable), PISA/TALIS honestly labeled as too heavy.
packs.summary: OECD skills and education microdata: PIAAC per-country CSVs are the usable sweet spot (open, no CORS via proxy); PISA and TALIS are open but far too heavy (hundreds of MB) — use OECD aggregate tables instead. Plus NAEP (US, restricted but NAEPprimer open for development), NCES longitudinal studies, the Urban Institute Education Data Portal API, IPEDS, College Scorecard, England's NPD-linked cohorts, Germany's NEPS, and the IEA family (TIMSS/PIRLS/ICILS/ICCS). Explains the plausible-values and replicate-weight rules that apply across the whole domain.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: Data catalogs and discovery engines (NADA/Dateno/CKAN/HF/Kaggle)
packs.description: How to search for microdata programmatically: catalog software families, cross-catalog search engines and government/ML data portals.
packs.summary: Discovery and catalog-search infrastructure, not a source of values itself: the NADA family (wbmicro/ihsn built-in adapters, plus the shared API behind ILO/FAO/UNHCR/WHO STEPS instances), Dateno and dataportals-registry for cross-catalog search, government open-data portals (CKAN, Socrata — cdc is a built-in example, data.europa.eu), ML hubs (hf and kaggle built-in adapters; OpenML/UCI), and social-science archives (ICPSR, UK Data Service, GESIS, CESSDA built-in adapter). Use to find where data lives before reading it through the app's own tools.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: Nordic registry microdata (Norway/Denmark/Sweden/Finland/Iceland)
packs.description: Individual-level Nordic population and health registries: microdata.no, Helsedata.no, and the Danish/Swedish/Finnish/Icelandic equivalents.
packs.summary: Norwegian, Danish, Swedish, Finnish and Icelandic register microdata: Norway's three access routes (microdata.no remote execution with its query language, Helsedata.no application costs/timelines, SSB data lending) and the health registries under it (NPR, KUHR, Reseptregisteret/NorPD, MFR, Dødsårsaksregisteret, Kreftregisteret, MoBa, CONOR, HUNT, Tromsø); Denmark (Forskermaskinen, Sundhedsdatastyrelsen); Sweden (MONA, Socialstyrelsen); Finland (Findata, THL); Iceland (Statistics Iceland, Landlæknir); the Nordic Commons policy vision. None of this is downloadable — always remote execution, enclave delivery, or application.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: European national statistics microdata, per country
packs.description: Per-country routes to official-statistics microdata across Europe, faster or richer than the central Eurostat process.
packs.summary: Per-country routes to European official-statistics microdata (distinct from the slower central Eurostat process): Germany (FDZ Destatis, IAB, FDZ-RV, GESIS MISSY), France (CASD, ADISP/Progedo), Netherlands (CBS Microdata, ODISSEI), UK (ONS SRS, UK Data Service, ADR UK), Italy and Spain (directly downloadable — the open exceptions), Austria (AMDC), Switzerland (BFS), Ireland (CSO RMF/ISSDA), Belgium/Portugal/Poland/Czechia/Greece, plus EU-level infrastructure (Eurostat safe centres, CESSDA, IZA IDSC, the not-yet-operative EHDS). Nordic countries are covered in the nordic-microdata pack.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: Labour market and firm microdata (LODES/QWI/IAB/firm registers)
packs.description: Worker, job, establishment and firm record-level data: openly downloadable US labour data plus European linked employer-employee sources.
packs.summary: Worker, job, establishment and firm microdata. US openly downloadable: LODES, QWI, BDS, CPS-ORG, QCEW, OEWS, JOLTS, O*NET, OSHA ITA, H-1B/PERM disclosure data; enclave-only: LBD/FSRDC. Europe: IAB SIAB/LIAB/BHP (JoSuA remote execution for non-residents), EU-LFS/SBS/CIS (aggregate open, microdata gated), open firm registers (GLEIF, UK Companies House, Norway's Enhetsregisteret, Denmark's CVR, Sweden's Bolagsverket), commercial ORBIS, EU-EFIGE and ECB SAFE/HFCS firm/household surveys, OECD MultiProd/DynEmp distributed computation, and the Nordic linked employer-employee registers.
packs.author: hans

packs.name: Demography, migration, housing and time use
packs.description: Population, mortality/fertility, migration, housing and time-use microdata, with an explicit warning on what is aggregate-only.
packs.summary: Population structure, mortality/fertility, migration, housing and time use. Warns which sources are aggregate-only (HMD/HFD/STMF, UN WPP, Eurostat demo_*/migr_*, OECD DIOC, every population grid) versus true microdata: census microdata (IPUMS International, UK/France/Spain national releases, US post-differential-privacy PPMF), migration surveys (UNHCR Microdata Library, IOM DTM, MAFE, MIGNEX), housing/consumption (ECB HFCS, Eurostat HBS, American Housing Survey, RECS, Consumer Expenditure Survey, UK Land Registry Price Paid), and time use (MTUS, HETUS, ATUS).
packs.author: hans

packs.name: Crime, transport, energy and political behaviour
packs.description: Crime/justice, transport safety, energy/environment exposure and political-behaviour microdata — the most openly-downloadable domain in this collection.
packs.summary: Crime/justice, transport safety, energy/environment exposure and political behaviour — the domain with the most openly-downloadable microdata: NCVS, NIBRS, FJC Integrated Database, Stanford Open Policing (crime); FARS, CRSS, NHTS, BTS DB1B (transport); EPA AQS, EEA air quality, ERA5/CAMS exposure layers, and the EJScreen removal (energy/environment); ANES, CES, MEDSL, CSES, Manifesto Project, ParlSpeech/ParlGov (politics); plus a closed-since-2023 digital-trace landscape (Reddit/Common Crawl/GDELT open, Twitter/CrowdTangle closed).
packs.author: hans

packs.name: Research data repositories (Dataverse/Zenodo)
packs.description: Replication and long-tail research data: Dataverse, Zenodo, OpenML and Figshare with access reality per platform.
packs.summary: Replication and long-tail research data: Zenodo (fully CORS-open, DOI-first) is cheapest to use; Dataverse (largest, ~300k datasets, needs proxy, expect 403s) and OpenML (ML benchmarks, exact-name lookup only) are usable; Figshare mostly skip (no CORS, signed URLs expire fast).
packs.author: hans
